patterns_data.top_pattern: GA authorized acute hospital spend is concentrated in three providers
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: GA / PPO Local / ACUTE HOSPITAL / authorized inpatient care
key_driver_codes: Other Disorders of Nervous System with CC
Other Circulatory System Diagnoses with CC
patterns_data.pattern_details: In GA, authorized PPO Local acute hospital spend is rising because volume is concentrated in a small set of hospitals, with added unit-cost pressure at two of them. MEMORIAL HEALTH UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER and NORTHSIDE HOSPITAL CHEROKEE show both more admissions and higher paid per admit, while PIEDMONT ATHENS REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER is mainly a volume story despite lower paid per admit. This is a provider concentration issue first, not a broad market-wide increase.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A few contracted hospitals are driving most of the increase, so targeted UM and reimbursement action can address a large share of the spend.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a joint UM, reimbursement, and network review on these three hospitals to test medical necessity, level-of-care management, and contract performance for the main nervous system, circulatory, liver, and musculoskeletal inpatient cases.
evidence_summary: MEMORIAL HEALTH UNIVERSITY MEDICAL CENTER added about +$2.4M with 114 more admissions and about +$2.3K paid per admit.
NORTHSIDE HOSPITAL CHEROKEE added about +$1.8M with 110 more admissions and about +$1.3K paid per admit.
PIEDMONT ATHENS REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER added about +$2.3M with 172 more admissions, even though paid per admit fell by about $2.2K.
Key inpatient drivers include Other Disorders of Nervous System with CC and Other Circulatory System Diagnoses with CC.

GA has about +$0.1M in a 'Not Mapped' facility bucket, and CA has another +$47K in the same bucket.
These findings are flagged as validation issues rather than confirmed operational change.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Outside acute hospitals, authorized PPO Local spend is also rising in SNF, critical access, and rehab settings. Some of this is clearly volume-led, especially in GA SNF and GA critical access, while CA SNF, PA SNF, and rehab settings add a unit-cost component. The business lever is site-of-care management across post-acute and lower-acuity facilities, not just acute inpatient controls.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If discharge routing, authorization criteria, or post-acute contracting are loose, spend can continue to migrate into non-acute settings even after acute hospital actions are taken.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Have UM and network teams jointly review discharge pathways, admission criteria, and contracted rates for SNF, critical access, and rehab settings in these segments, starting with GA and CA.
evidence_summary: CA SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$0.5M, including about 12 more admissions and roughly +$1.5K paid per admit.
GA CRITICAL ACCESS added about +$0.3M from 11 more admissions, while GA SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$0.3M from 20 more admissions.
PA and OH SNF - FREE STANDING added about +$0.2M combined with higher paid per admit in both settings.
NH Physical Rehab added about +$91K from 2 admissions at about $45.5K paid per admit.

patterns_data.pattern_details: CA and NY show a small number of very high-cost inpatient Med/Surg cases that materially lifted spend. The largest examples are a heart transplant or heart assist case at UCI MEDICAL CENTER and a spinal fusion case at NYU LANGONE HOSPITAL LONG ISLAND. This is not a broad utilization trend; it is a rare-case outlier pattern that needs case-level review.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A handful of catastrophic cases can materially move results and require different action than broad population management.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Send these cases to the clinical agent for case-level severity and appropriateness review, and confirm reimbursement terms for transplant and complex spine services.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The increase is driven by very small numbers of high-cost cases flagged as low-baseline and small-volume outliers.
evidence_summary: UCI MEDICAL CENTER had 1 heart transplant or heart assist case adding about +$288K.
NYU LANGONE HOSPITAL LONG ISLAND had 1 complex spinal fusion case adding about +$196K.
The remaining liver-related cases are much smaller and do not change the outlier-driven story.

The largest volume-led signal is sepsis and related circulatory admissions at PIEDMONT ATHENS REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER, while additional spend comes from neurologic, myopathy, myocarditis, and pericarditis cases in IP Med/Surg and NF. This mix suggests targeted clinical pathway and coding review is more appropriate than broad program changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Focused diagnosis clusters can often be managed through targeted clinical pathways, documentation review, and site-of-care management rather than system-wide interventions.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Send the GA diagnosis clusters to the clinical agent and UM operations for targeted review of sepsis admission drivers, neurologic rehabilitation pathways, and coding consistency on the emerging myocarditis, pericarditis, and myopathy cases.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Part of the pattern comes from low-baseline emerging diagnoses, so case identification and coding should be confirmed before broad action.
evidence_summary: PIEDMONT ATHENS REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER added about +$243K from 18 more sepsis-related admissions.
NF cases for Other Abnormalities Gait & Mobility and Unspecified Cord Compression added about +$145K and +$103K.
IP Med/Surg Critical Illness Myopathy added about +$132K across 5 admissions.
Additional rare IP Med/Surg myocarditis and pericarditis cases added about +$117K combined.
